crop.notes: Contains the 'To-Day's Programme' introduction under 'The Millers' through the start of the 'Tom Allen.' sketch heading. The biographical sketches and the rest of the article continue in the clipping for article 465.

ocr.notes: gist readable, many character errors (e.g. 'To-Law's Programme', 'Wash Home')

title.suggested: Allen and McCoole arrested on the eve of their second fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat previewed the second Allen–McCoole fight set for that day, reporting that both men had been arrested and released on $1,000 peace bonds by Judge Colvin of the Court of Criminal Correction.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Tuesday, September 23, 1873' and the masthead 'Daily Democrat'. This is before the 1875 merger, so it is not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen was arrested at 5 a.m. on Monday, September 22, 1873, hours after McCoole was arrested at his training quarters, ahead of their scheduled fight
Judge Colvin of the Court of Criminal Correction released Allen and McCoole on $1,000 bonds each to keep the peace in Missouri for three months; John Whelan signed Allen's bond

notes: Part one of a single long article; article 465 is its continuation (fight records, articles of agreement, scenes the night before). McCoole was described as entering the ring about 25 pounds heavier than Allen.
